stories.headline: Zelensky meets Trump at the White House to push an air truce and Patriot interceptors

key_facts.fact: Zelensky met Trump at the White House on July 28 to discuss a renewed diplomatic effort to end Russia's war, calling it 'a good meeting' and saying they discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor production.
key_facts.excerpt: "It was a good meeting," Zelensky said. "The President and I discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor production and several other ideas that could help."

key_facts.fact: The two leaders were expected to discuss a proposal for an air truce that would later be presented to Russia; a US official said both sides may now have incentives to accept an air ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: According to one person familiar with the matter, Zelensky and Trump were expected to discuss a proposal for an air truce that would later be presented to the Russian side... the White House believes both sides may now have incentives to accept an air ceasefire.

key_facts.fact: Moscow's mayor said the Russian capital was targeted by 390 drones in a matter of hours overnight before the meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky has arrived in the US at a significant stage in Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine, with Moscow's mayor saying the capital was targeted by 390 drones in a matter of hours overnight.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said on arrival that his 'number one priority' is 'anti-ballistic defense and strategic cooperation with America', and planned to meet senators at the Capitol on Tuesday evening after Sen. Lindsey Graham's funeral.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said in a social media post shortly after his arrival in the U.S. that his "number one priority" is "anti-ballistic defense and strategic cooperation with America."... Zelenskyy will head to the Capitol to meet with senators on Tuesday evening after Graham's funeral

key_facts.fact: Graham's final act as a public official was visiting Kyiv and securing agreement on a sanctions package targeting countries that buy Russian oil, gas and other exports; Congress is now weighing the bill.
key_facts.excerpt: Graham, whose final act as a public official was visiting Kyiv and securing an agreement on a package of sanctions that seek to punish countries that purchase Russian oil, gas and other exports.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones struck an export terminal at Rostov-on-Don, killing two and injuring five according to the regional governor, plus oil facilities in Udmurtia and Yaroslavl more than 1,300 km from Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Two people were killed in the attack on the port facility in Rostov-on-Don, and a further five injured, Rostov Oblast Governor Yury Slyusar reported the following morning. The attack also included strikes on oil facilities in Russia's Udmurtia Republic and Yaroslavl Oblast.

key_facts.fact: The Trump-Zelensky meeting was scheduled for 4:30 p.m. Moscow time, and all US senators were invited to talks with the Ukrainian president as Congress considers Russia sanctions legislation.
key_facts.excerpt: The meeting between Trump and Zelensky is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. Moscow time... All senators have also been invited to the talks with the Ukrainian president, which come as Congress considers a bill imposing sanctions on Russia.

stories.headline: Trump says Iran asked for the strike halt and sees a deal chance; Tehran denies talks exist

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Monday the US was having 'good talks' with Iran and there was a chance of a deal, warning strikes would resume if negotiations failed: 'if it doesn't, we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're having good talks," he said. "I think there's a good chance that something could happen, and if it does, good, if it doesn't, we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago."

key_facts.fact: At a Michigan rally Trump said of Iran: 'You can't bribe them. You've got to beat them, and we'll beat the hell out of them... Right now, there are very friendly negotiations going on.'
key_facts.excerpt: At a campaign rally in Michigan later on Monday, Trump said of Iran: "You can't bribe them. You've got to beat them, and we'll beat the hell out of them. But we'll see how it turns out. Right now, there are very friendly negotiations going on."

key_facts.fact: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said reports that Tehran had requested negotiations were 'fabricated', and that mediators may convey messages but there are no direct talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on Monday that messages were still being passed between the sides through mediators and Iran had not forsaken diplomacy, but reports that it requested negotiations were "fabricated."

key_facts.fact: Regional officials said mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan had made 'significant' progress and were working with Iran and Oman on a mechanism for managing vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: One of the regional officials who spoke to AP on Monday described the progress made in mediation efforts as "significant." He said mediators were working with Iran and Oman on a mechanism for managing vessels' transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq underscored the fragility of the pause, suggesting Iran-backed armed groups are testing the new US approach.
key_facts.excerpt: However, Iran has downplayed talk of negotiations, and its drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq underscored the fragility of the situation, suggesting that Tehran, or at least the Iran-backed armed groups around the region, is seeking to test the new US approach.

key_facts.fact: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Trump at the White House on Tuesday, his first in-person meeting with the president since the Iran war began in late February, on the day the war marked five months.
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu last came to Washington to meet with Trump in February, days before the U.S. entered into a months-long conflict with Iran. Tuesday officially marks five months of the war.

key_facts.fact: The 60-day interim deal signed in mid-June is well into its second half, with core issues including Iran's nuclear program set aside as mediators try to keep both sides talking.
key_facts.excerpt: The 60-day period established by the interim deal in mid-June is now well into its second half, and major issues that were meant to be negotiated — notably Iran's nuclear program at the heart of tensions — have been set aside as mediators try to keep both sides talking.

stories.headline: Seoul's Kospi crashes 10.8% and trips a circuit breaker as the global chip selloff deepens

key_facts.fact: The Kospi closed down 10.84% at 6,023.66, losing 732.09 points, after plunging as low as 5,830.39 during the session.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) lost 732.09 points, or 10.84 percent, to close at 6,023.66, after plunging to 5,830.39 at one point.

key_facts.fact: The exchange activated a sell-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m. — the 22nd this year — and a marketwide circuit breaker at 10:14 a.m. that halted Kospi trading for 20 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Heavy selling triggered a sell-side sidecar on the main bourse at 9:06 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange, marking the 22nd such sidecar this year. As losses deepened, a circuit breaker was activated at 10:14 a.m., halting trading for KOSPI-listed shares for 20 minutes.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics fell 13.39% to 220,000 won and SK hynix 14.65% to 1.55 million won; SK Square dropped 15.6% and Hyundai Motor 9.68%.
key_facts.excerpt: Market bellwether Samsung Electronics plummeted 13.39 percent to 220,000 won, and SK hynix nosedived 14.65 percent to 1.55 million won. SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, plunged 15.6 percent to 925,000 won

key_facts.fact: Foreign investors dumped a net 5 trillion won ($3.42 billion) of Kospi shares while retail investors bought a net 4.33 trillion won; the Kosdaq closed 7.7% lower at 705.85.
key_facts.excerpt: Foreign investors led the selloff, unloading a net 5 trillion won ($3.42 billion) in Kospi shares, while retail investors bought the dip with net purchases of 4.33 trillion won... The secondary Kosdaq also tumbled, hitting an intraday low of 697.45 before closing 7.7 percent lower at 705.85.

key_facts.fact: The Kospi had more than doubled from the start of the year to mid-June but has since lost around a third of its value.
key_facts.excerpt: The index had more than doubled from the start of the year to mid-June but has since lost around a third of its value.

key_facts.fact: Analysts tied the rout to a report that a Chinese firm is mass-producing immersion deep ultraviolet lithography machines and to Nvidia's reported $250 billion of financial guarantees for OpenAI's data center buildout.
key_facts.excerpt: "News that a Chinese company is producing immersion deep ultraviolet lithography equipment has raised concerns..." Lee added that reports of Nvidia providing $250 billion in financial guarantees related to OpenAI's data center investment had also shaken confidence in the AI investment cycle.

key_facts.fact: Korean financial authorities said they were considering additional measures to curb demand for single-stock leveraged ETFs tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, blamed for exacerbating volatility.
key_facts.excerpt: financial authorities said they were considering additional measures to curb demand for single-... exchange-traded funds (ETFs) linked to ... Electronics and SK hynix, which have been blamed for exacerbating market volatility.

stories.headline: Visa cuts about 2,600 jobs, 7% of staff, with AI reshaping how work gets done

key_facts.fact: Visa is eliminating about 2,600 jobs, roughly 7% of its workforce, primarily in technology and product teams, CEO Ryan McInerney said in a Tuesday staff memo.
key_facts.excerpt: Visa plans to cut 7% of its workforce, or about 2,600 jobs, a company spokesperson said on Tuesday, as the payments processor seeks to become more efficient... The job cuts will primarily affect technology and product teams.

key_facts.fact: McInerney told staff that AI is playing a key role: 'AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa.'
key_facts.excerpt: "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," McInerney wrote. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa."

key_facts.fact: Visa had about 34,100 employees at the end of its last fiscal year, more than triple the level of a decade earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Visa, which is set to report quarterly results after US markets close Tuesday, had about 34,100 employees at the end of its last fiscal year, more than triple from a decade earlier.

key_facts.fact: The company plans to reinvest in consumer payments, commercial and money-movement solutions and value-added services including stablecoin, cross-border and business-to-business offerings.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is making the cuts to reinvest in consumer payments, commercial and money movement solutions, and value-added services such as stablecoin, cross-border and B2B offerings, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: The cuts come about six months after a similar move by Visa's closest peer, with fintech rivals including PayPal and Block announcing even deeper reductions in recent months.
key_facts.excerpt: as the payments processor seeks to become more efficient, about six months after a similar move by its closest peer.

key_facts.fact: The layoffs were announced ahead of Visa's quarterly earnings release, with McInerney writing that 'we are entering a new era in commerce with a business that has real momentum'.
key_facts.excerpt: announced ahead of the company's quarterly earnings release, with McInerney saying Visa is entering a new phase of growth driven by strong financial performance, customer satisfaction and faster product development

stories.headline: FDA approves Freenome's blood test for colorectal cancer; Abbott owes a $100M milestone

key_facts.fact: On July 27, Freenome announced the FDA approved SimpleScreen CRC, a blood-based colorectal cancer screening option for average-risk adults aged 45 and older.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 27, 2026, the Company announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") has approved SimpleScreen™ CRC, a new blood-based screening option for colorectal cancer ("CRC") in adults 45 and older who are at average risk for the disease.

key_facts.fact: The test detects signals from cell-free DNA in blood and was validated in PREEMPT CRC, which enrolled more than 48,000 asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45-85 at over 200 sites.
key_facts.excerpt: SimpleScreen CRC detects signals associated with colorectal cancer from cell-free DNA in the blood... PREEMPT CRC enrolled more than 48,000 asymptomatic, average-risk adults between the ages of 45 and 85 who were scheduled for a screening colonoscopy.

key_facts.fact: In a prespecified US Census-adjusted analysis the test detected colorectal cancer with 81.1% sensitivity and advanced precancerous lesions with 13.7% sensitivity (30.7% for those with high-grade dysplasia), at 90.4% specificity for advanced colorectal neoplasia.
key_facts.excerpt: SimpleScreen CRC detected colorectal cancer with 81.1% sensitivity and advanced precancerous lesions ("APLs") with 13.7% sensitivity, including 30.7% for APLs with high-grade dysplasia. The test showed 90.4% specificity for advanced colorectal neoplasia.

key_facts.fact: Under an August 2025 agreement, Freenome will receive a $100 million milestone payment from Abbott, which will exclusively commercialize the test in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the commercial agreement signed between Freenome and Abbott in August 2025, Freenome will receive a $100 million milestone payment from Abbott for this FDA approval. Abbott will exclusively commercialize SimpleScreen CRC in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: Approval means the test meets Medicare coverage criteria and is expected to be named in American Cancer Society guidelines; up to 60 million Americans remain overdue for recommended colorectal screening.
key_facts.excerpt: With FDA approval, SimpleScreen CRC meets the coverage criteria for Medicare and is expected to be incorporated into the American Cancer Society guidelines by name... Up to 60 million Americans remain overdue for recommended screening.

key_facts.fact: Freenome trades on Nasdaq as FRNM after a combination with Perceptive Capital Solutions Corp, and is led by CEO Aaron Elliott.

stories.headline: EPA says off-grid power plants built for data centers escape Clean Air Act acid rain rules

key_facts.fact: The EPA announced on July 27 that the Clean Air Act's Acid Rain Program does not apply to 'islanded' power generation facilities that are not connected to a public electricity grid.
key_facts.excerpt: This month, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) issued guidance clarifying that the Clean Air Act (CAA) Acid Rain Program (ARP) does not apply to power generation facilities that are not connected to a public electricity grid, commonly referred to as "islanded" power generation facilities.

key_facts.fact: The agency said the guidance 'expands opportunities for companies to develop and operate islanded power generation facilities for data centers', giving developers more flexibility in where and how quickly they build.
key_facts.excerpt: The guidance expands opportunities for companies to develop and operate islanded power generation facilities for data centers. This will give developers greater flexibility in where and how quickly they can build new facilities

key_facts.fact: EPA Assistant Administrator Aaron Szabo wrote in a July 16 letter that 'the Acid Rain Program does not apply to power generation facilities that are not connected in any way to the larger electricity grid.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The EPA believes that, considering the plain text of these definitions, the Acid Rain Program does not apply to power generation facilities that are not connected in any way to the larger electricity grid," EPA Assistant Administrator Aaron Szabo wrote in a July 16 letter.

key_facts.fact: The Acid Rain Program, created by the 1990 Clean Air Act amendments, caps sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide emissions from large fossil-fired power plants and has been central to cutting smog and soot.
key_facts.excerpt: The Acid Rain Program was established under the 1990 amendments to the Clean Air Act to reduce emissions of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from large fossil fuel-fired power plants.

key_facts.fact: EPA said the program applies to facilities that sell electricity or must report as a generating unit to the Department of Energy; if an islanded plant later connects to the grid it may become subject to the rules.
key_facts.excerpt: the ARP applies to facilities that sell electricity or are required to report as a generating unit to the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)... If a company develops a power generation facility that is not grid connected, but at a future date the company does connect the facility to the grid, the facility may be subject to the provisions in the ARP.

key_facts.fact: EPA cast the guidance as insulating ratepayers from costs tied to surging data center power demand, and framed it as reducing strain on regional electric grids.
key_facts.excerpt: EPA cast the guidance as an effort to insulate ratepayers from the costs associated with increased power demand from data center build-out.

stories.headline: MapLight's muscarinic pill hits its Phase 2 goal in schizophrenia and improves cognition

key_facts.fact: MapLight Therapeutics said on July 27 that its Phase 2 ZEPHYR trial met its primary endpoint, with the 210/3 mg twice-daily dose cutting PANSS total score versus placebo at Week 5 (LS mean difference -4.5, p=0.015, effect size 0.37).
key_facts.excerpt: The trial, designed and sized to support registration, met its primary endpoint, with the 210/3 mg BID dose demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in PANSS total score compared to placebo at Week 5 with an effect size of 0.37 (LS mean difference vs PBO -4.5, p=0.015)

key_facts.fact: ML-007C-MA is an oral M1/M4 muscarinic agonist (betovumeline) co-formulated with the peripherally acting anticholinergic fesoterodine, designed to limit peripheral cholinergic side effects.
key_facts.excerpt: ML-007C-MA is an oral, extended-release, fixed-dose combination of the investigational M1/M4 muscarinic agonist ML-007 (betovumeline), co-formulated with a peripherally acting anticholinergic (fesoterodine).

key_facts.fact: Patients with baseline cognitive impairment showed improved cognitive performance on a prespecified secondary endpoint (effect size 0.51, p=0.041), an effect the company says was independent of antipsychotic response.
key_facts.excerpt: based on the pre-specified secondary endpoint assessed via the Cogstate battery in participants with baseline cognitive impairment (effect size=0.51; 0.44 points versus placebo; p=0.041). This cognitive benefit did not demonstrate correlation with the change in PANSS score

key_facts.fact: ZEPHYR randomized 307 inpatient adults with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia 1:1:1 across 25 US sites; the 330/6 mg once-daily arm improved numerically but missed statistical significance on the primary endpoint.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 307 participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive either placebo, ML-007C-MA 210/3 mg twice daily, or ML-007C-MA 330/6 mg once daily... The 330/6 mg once-daily (QD) dose... demonstrated numerical improvement over placebo, but did not achieve statistical significance on the primary endpoint.

key_facts.fact: No serious or drug-related severe adverse events occurred with either dose; all-cause discontinuation across the active arms was 19.9%, and gastrointestinal events caused discontinuation in only two patients (2.0%).
key_facts.excerpt: there were no serious adverse events or drug-related severe TEAEs with either dose... All-cause discontinuation across both active arms was low, at 19.9%. ... Gastrointestinal events were mostly mild and rarely associated with discontinuation (two participants, 2.0%)

key_facts.fact: The Nasdaq-listed company plans an End-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting and a second registrational trial to replicate the result before an NDA; its VISTA trial in Alzheimer's disease psychosis reads out in the second half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Company plans to engage with the FDA at an End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting to discuss the path forward... VISTA, MapLight's ongoing trial designed to support registration for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer's disease psychosis... with topline results expected in the second half of 2027.

sources.title: MapLight Therapeutics Announces Positive Topline Results from Phase 2 ZEPHYR Trial of ML-007C-MA in Schizophrenia
